pathway.title: Upbound Group, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage is moderate and falling, but the fall rests on cash rather than earnings. Net debt to EBITDA went from 4.05x at FY2025 to 3.05x at 2026-09-30 (3.11x pro forma for the dividend paid on 2026-10-27) as net debt fell 15.66% and last-twelve-months EBITDA rose 12.05%. Operating cash flow was USD 457.1 million in nine months against USD 264.0 million, with free cash flow at 108.18% of EBITDA against 66.73% in FY2025, helped by a USD 35.1 million tax refund and lower merchandise purchases, so part of the paydown reverses if Acima volume recovers. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56

- Liquidity and maturities leave about two years of runway. Revolver availability is USD 451.2 million against identified twelve-month cash calls of USD 195.10 million (43.24% of availability), nothing is printed as due before 2029, and the 2029 maturities of USD 495 million are 36.36% of principal while the term loan of USD 866.25 million runs to 2032. Springing maturity terms are not supplied, so the dates are contractual rather than tested. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-04; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

- Interest cover is the thinnest metric. EBITDA covered cash interest 3.40x in FY2025 against 3.78x in FY2024, 66.94% of principal is floating, one percentage point is worth USD 9.1 million a year and the term loan rate rose to 6.83% by 2026-10-22 from 6.48% at 2026-09-30. Cover of that size leaves little room if EBITDA falls or rates rise together. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-02; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62

- Business risk centres on Acima. It supplies 52.05% of revenue and 51.95% of segment operating profit, its volume fell 9.3% in nine months and 11.0% in the third quarter, and its margin rose to 12.27% from 11.66% only because fewer customers used early purchase options. Rent-A-Center is stable but contracting and Brigit adds 6.17% of revenue with rising advance losses, so diversification is real but not yet large enough to offset an Acima decline. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-05; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56

- Legal exposure is the largest claim outside debt. Estimated accruals are USD 57.9 million, down 19.58% since year-end, a settlement with the multistate group of 43 states is only agreed in principle, and no range is estimated for unaccrued matters; USD 37.5 million of Brigit deferred consideration and an earnout of up to USD 60 million add further cash claims. A settlement above the accrual or conduct remedies at Acima would reach both liquidity and the main profit source. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-03; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9

- Secured lenders rank ahead of the notes and the structure is only partly visible. Secured principal of USD 911.25 million is 2.27x of EBITDA and total principal 3.40x, the USD 450 million notes are unsecured and structurally behind non-guarantor subsidiaries, and guarantor names are not supplied, so recovery work belongs to Structural priority and Recovery & fulcrum rather than this module. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-04; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23

- Financial policy is shareholder-leaning but not creditor-adverse. Dividends paid were 119.97% of FY2025 net earnings and 75.81% in nine months of 2026, the USD 235.0 million repurchase authorisation is unused, and no sponsor, priming or debt-funded distribution is documented; payout capacity under the debt documents is not established. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-07; 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 89

- The primary downside path is a further Acima volume fall coinciding with a settlement above the accrual. Replaying the FY2025 EBITDA decline of 12.76% lifts net leverage to 3.50x (3.56x pro forma), each USD 100 million of unplanned cash cost adds 0.25x, and interest cover is the first metric to break, while liquidity would still cover the identified calls. Basis: calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-02

cells.text: Lease-to-own provider to underserved consumers through the Acima (third-party retailer, virtual and staffed) and Rent-A-Center (stores and e-commerce) segments, plus the Brigit financial-health application and company-owned stores in Mexico
Weekly to monthly lease payments with no long-term obligation; ownership mostly through early purchase options; Brigit earns subscription, expedited-transfer and marketplace fees
Revenue 1,836,943 thousand in 9M 2026 (52.05% of revenue); thousands of retailer locations; virtual and staffed kiosks with minimal capital expenditure; volume down 9.3%
Revenue 1,407,031 thousand in 9M 2026 (39.87%); 1,943 locations at 2026-09-30 including 304 franchise stores; e-commerce 28% of lease-to-own revenue
Revenue 217,589 thousand in 9M 2026 (6.17%); earned wage access advances, credit builder and subscriptions; acquired 2025-01-31
Ashley Furniture Industries, LG Electronics and Whirlpool were 37%, 11% and 10% of 2025 merchandise purchases; no minimum-purchase contracts
First quarter strongest because tax refunds drive early purchase options; cash for merchandise purchases is spread across the year
Other lease-to-own operators, retailers and online sellers, buy-now-pay-later and subprime lenders; Brigit faces other earned wage access and credit-building providers

Rental purchase statutes in 46 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico; courts in Wisconsin and New Jersey treat the transaction as a credit sale; federal consumer-finance enforcement; state rules on earned wage access
12,050 coworkers at 2025-12-31: 10,290 in the United States and Puerto Rico, 1,050 in Mexico and 710 at corporate
Grow Acima retailer penetration, grow Brigit products, shift Rent-A-Center to e-commerce and use data analytics; management describes the company as a "technology and data-driven leader"

runs.text: The five strengths are, in rank order: moderate and falling calculated leverage, because net debt over EBITDA is 3.05x (3.11x pro forma for the dividend paid on 2026-10-27) against 4.05x at FY2025, which lowers default risk and creates room for legal and deferred claims; no bullet maturity before 2029, because the printed schedule shows nothing due earlier apart from small term loan installments, which defers refinancing risk; revolver availability of USD 451.2 million, which covers identified cash calls; two scaled lease-to-own platforms plus a growing fintech segment that diversify revenue sources; and no controlling sponsor identified, so no owner is positioned to extract value beyond board-set dividends. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-05

The five weaknesses are, in rank order: Acima volume decline, which shrinks the largest profit source and reverses the current cash release; a legal and regulatory overhang whose settlement cash and conduct terms are not fully accrued; thin interest cover of 3.40x on 66.94% floating-rate principal; a concentrated 2029 refinancing of USD 495 million against springing maturity terms that are not supplied; and dividends above FY2025 earnings that compete with debt reduction. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-04

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The Brigit acquisition closed on 2025-01-31 for total purchase consideration of about USD 395.4 million: cash of 70.23%, stock of 10.37% and deferred and contingent consideration of 19.40%. A portion of the cash was financed with additional debt, the first installment of USD 37.5 million of the USD 75 million deferred consideration was paid in 2026, and the remainder is due by 2027-Q1 along with an earnout of up to USD 60 million based on 2026 results. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-09

New debt in the period was limited to amendments: the fourth term loan amendment on 2025-08-19 extended maturity to 2032 and added about USD 77 million of borrowings, and the third ABL amendment on 2025-08-29 changed covenants that are not described. No new debt issue or amendment is dated in 2026 in the five filings, and the senior notes due 2029, issued in 2021, remain the only unsecured debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 152; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt to EBITDA was 4.05x at FY2025, the highest of the five balance sheet dates examined, and has since fallen to 3.05x, with total debt to EBITDA falling from 4.39x to 3.36x on the same calculated EBITDA. Both legs of the ratio moved: net debt at 2026-09-30 is 15.66% below year-end, and last-twelve-months EBITDA is 12.05% above FY2025. The FY2025 peak came from the debt-funded Brigit acquisition lifting net debt 16.06%, while EBITDA fell 12.76% as other gains and charges rose 102.93% to 4.52% of revenue. For creditors the path matters as much as the level: the March and June 2026 readings of 3.56x and 3.46x show a steady paydown rather than a single-quarter move.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The deleveraging came from cash, not from earnings. Operating cash flow for nine months of 2026 was USD 457.1 million against USD 264.0 million a year earlier, up 73.15%, while the cash outflow for rental merchandise fell 12.14% and a tax refund of USD 35.1 million arrived. The lower merchandise purchases follow a 9.3% fall in Acima gross merchandise volume, so part of the cash release reflects buying less merchandise for a shrinking Acima book, and it reverses if volume recovers. Free cash flow was 108.18% of last-twelve-months EBITDA against 66.73% in FY2025 and 11.82% in FY2024, which is not a run rate; after Brigit customer cash advances it is 88.33%.

fields.value: EBITDA covered cash interest 3.40x in FY2025 against 3.78x in FY2024, because EBITDA fell 12.76% while cash interest paid fell only 2.97%. Cash interest paid is printed only in the annual reports, so interim cover is not calculable; on accrued interest expense, last-twelve-months cover is 3.80x against 3.17x in FY2025, and cover after capital expenditure was 2.76x in FY2025 against 3.26x in FY2024. With 66.94% of principal at floating rates and cover below 4x, creditors are exposed to rate moves: the filing puts a one percentage point change at USD 9.1 million of annual pre-tax interest, and the term loan rate had risen to 6.83% by 2026-10-22 from 6.48% at 2026-09-30.

fields.value: In nine months of 2026 operating cash flow of USD 457.1 million funded dividends of USD 69.5 million, capital expenditure of USD 47.6 million, customer cash advances net of collections of USD 69.0 million and the first USD 37.5 million Brigit deferred installment, and still left room to repay debt: repayments of USD 485.6 million exceeded new borrowing of USD 260.0 million. Customer advances are an investing outflow that behaves like Brigit working capital, so free cash flow after them is the better measure of what is available to creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was cash of USD 125.1 million plus ABL availability of USD 451.2 million after USD 53.8 million of letters of credit, 0.43x of total debt against 0.23x at FY2025. By 2026-10-22 cash was USD 73.5 million and availability USD 456.2 million. Calls on that liquidity are the dividend paid 2026-10-27, the remaining USD 37.5 million of Brigit deferred consideration due no later than 30 days after the second anniversary of the 2025-01-31 closing, term loan installments of USD 8.75 million a year and estimated legal accruals of USD 57.9 million that include a non-binding agreement in principle with the multistate attorneys general. Availability is the filing's figure: the borrowing base is not printed, and use of the full amount depends on a fixed charge coverage maintenance covenant whose level is not stated. No facility expires within twelve months of 2026-09-30; the nearest maturity is the notes on 2029-02-15.

Its fall of USD 9.9 million in nine months is a small cash use consistent with a smaller lease book, not a sign of stress.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt at 2026-09-30 is three instruments with USD 1,361.25 million of principal: the ABL with USD 45.0 million drawn of USD 550 million of commitments, due 2029-06-07; the term loan with USD 866.25 million, due 2032-08-19; and USD 450 million of 6.375% senior notes due 2029-02-15. Nothing is printed as maturing before 2029, so the wall is USD 495 million in 2029 (the notes and the ABL drawings) and USD 866.25 million in 2032, but the term loan's 1.00% annual amortization of USD 8.75 million is stated in the notes and absent from the maturity table. Springing maturity provisions apply to both bank facilities and their terms are not supplied, so the 2029 and 2032 dates are contractual, not tested.

fields.value: The ABL and the term loan are secured on separate collateral pools, each first-priority on its own pool, so both carry rank 1 here and holders of the notes sit behind USD 911.25 million of secured principal, 2.27x of EBITDA. The notes are unsecured, effectively subordinated to that debt and structurally subordinated to subsidiaries that do not guarantee them; cumulative leverage through the notes is 3.40x on principal against 3.36x on carrying value. The borrower named in the 2021 credit agreements is Rent-A-Center, Inc., the indenture is listed between Radiant Funding SPV, LLC and Truist Bank, and no guarantor is named, so the obligor at each rank is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | What the company does | Lease-to-own provider to underserved consumers through the Acima (third-party retailer, virtual and staffed) and Rent-A-Center (stores and e-commerce) segments, plus the Brigit financial-health application and company-owned stores in Mexico | 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9 |

fields.value: | Revenue model | Weekly to monthly lease payments with no long-term obligation; ownership mostly through early purchase options; Brigit earns subscription, expedited-transfer and marketplace fees | 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12 |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business & governance for Upbound Group, Inc. (issuer id upbd-933036) as of 2026-11-18 on the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope: business and operating model, ownership and control, governance, sponsor and shareholder behaviour and transaction history, from the five supplied SEC filings through the quarter ended 2026-09-30. Financial figures are taken from the filings directly and are not Financial foundation outputs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Upbound is a public, scaled lease-to-own operator with no identified controlling sponsor, so creditors rely on debt-document protections and cash generation rather than owner support, and the dominant business risks are falling Acima volume and unresolved state attorney general matters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acima supplies 52.05% of nine-month 2026 revenue and 51.95% of segment operating profit while its merchandise volume fell 9.3%; Rent-A-Center adds 39.87% of revenue from a shrinking store base, and Brigit, at 6.17% of revenue, is growing with rising advance losses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is mixed rather than adverse: dividends paid in FY2025 were 119.97% of net earnings and the Brigit purchase was partly debt-funded, yet no liability management, priming or debt-funded recapitalisation is documented. Ownership, board and related-party detail sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so the sponsor and governance risk level is Medium on incomplete evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue and profit are concentrated in Acima, whose retailer-channel volume is now shrinking. Acima was 53.51% of FY2025 revenue and 50.80% of segment operating profit; its volume fell 9.3% in nine months and 11.0% in the third quarter, and revenue fell 2.37%. Margin held at 12.27% against 11.66% because fewer customers used early purchase options and lease charge-offs eased to 8.8% of revenue from 9.3%, so profit is being protected by mix rather than growth. Lower volume releases merchandise cash today but shrinks the base that services the debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Rent-A-Center is a large but contracting store franchise. Store count fell 5.92% in nine months, 69 stores were closed in the second quarter, revenue slipped 0.72% and segment margin fell to 12.26% from 13.11% as lease charge-offs rose to 5.0% of revenue from 4.7%. The closures are intended to lower fixed cost, but the savings are not quantified, so creditors should treat the segment as stable cash generation with no growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-02; 10-Q_2026-06-30_upbd-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Brigit adds growth and margin but a different, more regulated credit risk. Revenue rose 53.87% (part of that is nine months against eight months) at a 16.05% segment margin, while net advance losses reached 3.9% of advances against 2.8%, and the advances are funded from consolidated cash with no matched funding disclosed. Regulation of earned wage access is changing state by state, so the segment can add earnings but also event risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-02; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Regulatory and legal exposure is the main source of claims outside debt and of earnings volatility. Estimated legal accruals were USD 57.9 million, down 19.58% since year-end; a non-binding agreement in principle exists with the multistate group of 43 states, and on 2026-08-27 the court let the New York Attorney General's case proceed except for one allegation, with settlement talks active. Any settlement above the accrual, or injunctive terms that change Acima's practices, would reach the largest profit source, and no range is estimated for unaccrued matters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CALC-07; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management has been refreshed at the top and governance detail is not supplied. The Chief Executive Officer role passed on 2025-06-01 to the former Chief Financial Officer, a new Chief Financial Officer joined on 2025-11-10 and a Chief Growth Officer on 2025-09-18, while the auditor changed to Deloitte & Touche LLP for FY2025 with no disagreements reported and Brigit excluded from the internal control assessment. New finance leadership during settlements and integration raises execution risk, which creditors should monitor through reporting quality rather than assume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Shareholder distributions are modest in relation to cash flow (36.81% of FY2025 operating cash flow less capital expenditure) but exceeded earnings in FY2025, and acquisitions have been debt-assisted with no creditor-adverse transaction documented. Dividends paid were 119.97% of FY2025 net earnings and 75.81% in nine months of 2026, the annual run rate at the current share count is USD 90.95 million, and no repurchase has occurred since 2023 although USD 235.0 million of authorisation remains. The Brigit deal left USD 37.5 million of deferred consideration and an earnout of up to USD 60 million outside debt. Distribution and acquisition capacity cannot be tested because the debt documents are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-09; 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Supply and control terms are secondary vulnerabilities. Three suppliers account for 58% of merchandise purchases with no minimum-purchase contracts, a cybersecurity incident drove fraudulent lease contracts of about USD 13.3 million in the second quarter of 2026 with the investigation ongoing, and a third party acquiring 40% of the votes is an event of default under the bank facilities. These raise operating and control-change risk but do not by themselves threaten debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-11; 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_upbd-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 81

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that the earnings engine is improving: Acima's segment operating profit rose 2.74% on lower volume, Rent-A-Center remains profitable, Brigit adds a high-margin segment, legal accruals fell 19.58% and the company carries no sponsor that could extract value. Distributions fell to 75.81% of net earnings in nine months of 2026 and no creditor-adverse transaction is documented.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: That reading would win if Acima volume stabilised, the multistate and New York matters settled within the accrued amount without changes to Acima's practices, and the proxy statement and credit agreements showed independent directors and tight restricted-payment baskets. The cautious view would strengthen if a settlement exceeded the accrual, fraud losses recurred, Brigit advance losses kept rising or the dividend were maintained while earnings fell below it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-07; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Beneficial ownership, board composition, compensation and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so the finding that no controlling sponsor exists and the Medium sponsor and governance risk level are provisional and would change if a large holder or fee arrangement appears.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreements and indenture are not supplied, so the dividend, acquisition and priming capacity behind the financial-policy finding is not tested, and the absence of liability management rests on a text search of the filings only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No retailer or customer concentration for Acima is printed, so the concern about revenue durability rests on volume and margin trends alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Form 8-K on the cybersecurity incidents is not supplied, so the fraud-loss run-rate beyond the second quarter is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Segment margins exclude corporate costs of 53.24% of segment operating profit in nine months of 2026, and the Brigit growth rate compares nine months with eight, so segment results overstate consolidated profitability and growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Legal accruals cover only matters judged probable and no range is estimated for the rest, so the legal exposure conclusion is a lower bound.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Brigit acquisition closed on 2025-01-31 for total purchase consideration of about USD 395.4 million: cash of 70.23%, stock of 10.37% and deferred and contingent consideration of 19.40%. A portion of the cash was financed with additional debt, the first installment of USD 37.5 million of the USD 75 million deferred consideration was paid in 2026, and the remainder is due by 2027-Q1 along with an earnout of up to USD 60 million based on 2026 results.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt in the period was limited to amendments: the fourth term loan amendment on 2025-08-19 extended maturity to 2032 and added about USD 77 million of borrowings, and the third ABL amendment on 2025-08-29 changed covenants that are not described. No new debt issue or amendment is dated in 2026 in the five filings, and the senior notes due 2029, issued in 2021, remain the only unsecured debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. The level is driven by dividends above FY2025 earnings, debt-assisted acquisitions with deferred claims and an open legal settlement overhang, because each competes with debt reduction or adds claims outside debt, which implies slower deleveraging if earnings weaken. Countervailing evidence is the fall of dividends to 75.81% of nine-month earnings, no repurchases since 2023, no documented creditor-adverse transaction and no controlling owner able to extract value. Further analysis requires the proxy statement and the executed debt documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is moderate and falling, but the fall rests on cash rather than earnings. Net debt to EBITDA went from 4.05x at FY2025 to 3.05x at 2026-09-30 (3.11x pro forma for the dividend paid on 2026-10-27) as net debt fell 15.66% and last-twelve-months EBITDA rose 12.05%. Operating cash flow was USD 457.1 million in nine months against USD 264.0 million, with free cash flow at 108.18% of EBITDA against 66.73% in FY2025, helped by a USD 35.1 million tax refund and lower merchandise purchases, so part of the paydown reverses if Acima volume recovers.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity and maturities leave about two years of runway. Revolver availability is USD 451.2 million against identified twelve-month cash calls of USD 195.10 million (43.24% of availability), nothing is printed as due before 2029, and the 2029 maturities of USD 495 million are 36.36% of principal while the term loan of USD 866.25 million runs to 2032. Springing maturity terms are not supplied, so the dates are contractual rather than tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-04; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Interest cover is the thinnest metric. EBITDA covered cash interest 3.40x in FY2025 against 3.78x in FY2024, 66.94% of principal is floating, one percentage point is worth USD 9.1 million a year and the term loan rate rose to 6.83% by 2026-10-22 from 6.48% at 2026-09-30. Cover of that size leaves little room if EBITDA falls or rates rise together.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-02; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Business risk centres on Acima. It supplies 52.05% of revenue and 51.95% of segment operating profit, its volume fell 9.3% in nine months and 11.0% in the third quarter, and its margin rose to 12.27% from 11.66% only because fewer customers used early purchase options. Rent-A-Center is stable but contracting and Brigit adds 6.17% of revenue with rising advance losses, so diversification is real but not yet large enough to offset an Acima decline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-05; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Legal exposure is the largest claim outside debt. Estimated accruals are USD 57.9 million, down 19.58% since year-end, a settlement with the multistate group of 43 states is only agreed in principle, and no range is estimated for unaccrued matters; USD 37.5 million of Brigit deferred consideration and an earnout of up to USD 60 million add further cash claims. A settlement above the accrual or conduct remedies at Acima would reach both liquidity and the main profit source.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-03; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Secured lenders rank ahead of the notes and the structure is only partly visible. Secured principal of USD 911.25 million is 2.27x of EBITDA and total principal 3.40x, the USD 450 million notes are unsecured and structurally behind non-guarantor subsidiaries, and guarantor names are not supplied, so recovery work belongs to Structural priority and Recovery & fulcrum rather than this module.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-04; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy is shareholder-leaning but not creditor-adverse. Dividends paid were 119.97% of FY2025 net earnings and 75.81% in nine months of 2026, the USD 235.0 million repurchase authorisation is unused, and no sponsor, priming or debt-funded distribution is documented; payout capacity under the debt documents is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-07; 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 89

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The primary downside path is a further Acima volume fall coinciding with a settlement above the accrual. Replaying the FY2025 EBITDA decline of 12.76% lifts net leverage to 3.50x (3.56x pro forma), each USD 100 million of unplanned cash cost adds 0.25x, and interest cover is the first metric to break, while liquidity would still cover the identified calls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against an adequate and improving view is that the improvement is largely cash timing: free cash flow of 108.18% of EBITDA includes a tax refund and a working-capital release that reverse when merchandise purchases normalise, LTM EBITDA margin of 8.48% is still below the 9.49% of FY2024, and the 2029 wall of USD 495 million meets springing maturity terms that are not supplied. If those terms bring bank maturities forward, the refinancing event arrives earlier than the printed dates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The case for a stronger view is that EBITDA itself recovered: third-quarter EBITDA was 22.77% above the prior year, interest expense is 6.65% lower than in FY2025, and adding back other gains and charges gives net leverage of 2.49x, for which a pro forma figure after the dividend is not established. The view would turn clearly positive if Acima volume stabilised and the legal matters settled within the accrual; it would turn negative if net leverage rose above 3.56x, ABL availability fell without a matching rise in cash, or the dividend continued while earnings fell below it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No rating, agency view or market price is supplied, so the refinancing-capacity conclusion rests on maturity timing and liquidity alone and would weaken if the notes trade at a discount or ratings fall; the 2025 annual report states only that the debt is rated below investment grade.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant levels, the borrowing base and the executed debt documents are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not established and the liquidity conclusion is the filing's availability figure rather than a recomputation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The sources contain no management projection or guidance, so the outlook and downside are arithmetic sensitivities on reported figures and not forecasts; a different Acima volume path would change the leverage and cover conclusions directly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer data are supplied, so whether the profile is better or worse than typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - EBITDA is calculated from statement lines by Financial foundation and is struck after depreciation of rental merchandise, so a lender definition that adds back other items would lower every leverage ratio quoted here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five strengths are, in rank order: moderate and falling calculated leverage, because net debt over EBITDA is 3.05x (3.11x pro forma for the dividend paid on 2026-10-27) against 4.05x at FY2025, which lowers default risk and creates room for legal and deferred claims; no bullet maturity before 2029, because the printed schedule shows nothing due earlier apart from small term loan installments, which defers refinancing risk; revolver availability of USD 451.2 million, which covers identified cash calls; two scaled lease-to-own platforms plus a growing fintech segment that diversify revenue sources; and no controlling sponsor identified, so no owner is positioned to extract value beyond board-set dividends.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five weaknesses are, in rank order: Acima volume decline, which shrinks the largest profit source and reverses the current cash release; a legal and regulatory overhang whose settlement cash and conduct terms are not fully accrued; thin interest cover of 3.40x on 66.94% floating-rate principal; a concentrated 2029 refinancing of USD 495 million against springing maturity terms that are not supplied; and dividends above FY2025 earnings that compete with debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Upbound leases durable goods to consumers who do not qualify for traditional credit, through Acima retailer locations and Rent-A-Center stores, and adds earned wage access and subscriptions through Brigit. Customers pay weekly to monthly with no long-term obligation and mostly take ownership through early purchase options, so revenue visibility is short and depends on renewals and charge-offs rather than on contracts. That gives quick cash conversion but leaves creditors exposed to consumer payment behaviour and to the pace of merchandise purchases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is listed common stock with no controlling holder identified, and the board sets dividends within limits in the debt agreements. A third party reaching 40% of the votes is an event of default under the bank facilities, so control change is protected, but sponsor support cannot be assumed and ownership concentration is not established because the proxy statement is not supplied. Business & governance assesses sponsor and governance risk as Medium on incomplete evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 178

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is recurring in form but discretionary and volume-sensitive. Acima volume fell 9.3% in nine months and revenue 2.37%, Rent-A-Center revenue is flat as stores close, and Brigit grew from a small base, so the durable base is Rent-A-Center rentals while Acima carries the growth and the risk. Three suppliers account for 58% of merchandise purchases with no minimum-purchase contracts, which adds a supply dependency without contractual protection.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-05; 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins have been defended by loss control rather than by price. LTM EBITDA margin is 8.48% against 9.49% in FY2024 and 7.62% in FY2025; Acima margin rose to 12.27% because fewer customers used early purchase options and charge-offs eased, while Rent-A-Center charge-offs rose. Cost flexibility is real in merchandise purchases, which fell 12.14% as a cash outflow, but occupancy and labor are largely fixed, so a volume fall deleverages operating profit quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-05; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditure is light at 1.42% of FY2025 revenue, so conversion depends on rental merchandise purchases inside operating cash flow. Free cash flow was 11.82% of EBITDA in FY2024, 66.73% in FY2025 and 108.18% on a last-twelve-months basis, which shows volatility more than a level, and cash taxes and the excess cash flow sweep on the term loan from fiscal 2026 will reduce what is retained. Creditors should therefore size debt service on EBITDA and interest cover, not on the current free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-03; 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 155

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is high: Upbound competes with other lease-to-own operators, retailers, buy-now-pay-later providers and subprime lenders, and Brigit competes with other earned wage access and credit-building providers, which caps pricing and rewards loss discipline. Buyers, the Acima retailers, hold bargaining power that cannot be sized because retailer concentration is not printed, suppliers are concentrated at 58% of purchases for three names, and new entrants and substitutes arrive through fintech and online channels. The credit consequence is that margin gains must come from loss control and volume, not price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulation is a primary credit driver and is treated as the material external factor: state rental purchase statutes, consumer-finance enforcement against Acima, and evolving state rules on earned wage access directly set legal cash costs and the terms on which Acima and Brigit can operate. Economic conditions matter through consumer payment behaviour and short-term rates, since 66.94% of principal floats; social and technology factors are not primary credit drivers on the supplied evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation CALC-02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In credit terms, strengths are leverage that has fallen, a long maturity runway, revolver availability, scale across two platforms and the absence of a sponsor; weaknesses are Acima's shrinking volume, thin cover, legal exposure and a concentrated 2029 refinancing; opportunities that would improve quality are stabilising Acima volume, settlements within the accrual and Brigit growth at stable losses; threats are higher rates, unaccrued settlement cash or conduct remedies, and a springing maturity that arrives early.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are average: revenue growth was 8.67% in FY2025, but no market share data are supplied and the largest segment is shrinking. Competitive advantage is average, resting on the Acima retailer network and the Rent-A-Center brand, with no moat evidence beyond management language. Business diversification is average because Acima is 52.05% of revenue and 51.95% of segment profit. Cost and capex flexibility is average, since merchandise purchases fell 12.14% and capital expenditure is 1.42% of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin stability is average, with EBITDA margin between 7.62% and 9.49% over three periods; free cash flow stability is weak, because free cash flow moved from 11.82% to 108.18% of EBITDA. Ability to refinance is average: nothing is due before 2029 and the term loan runs to 2032, but the debt is rated below investment grade, USD 495 million falls due in 2029 and springing terms are unseen. Liquidity is average: availability of USD 451.2 million gives liquidity equal to 0.43x of total debt, but the borrowing base and covenant level are not printed. Financial policy and governance is average, with dividends above FY2025 earnings offset by no sponsor and no documented creditor-adverse transaction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-07; 10-K_2025-12-31_upbd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are lower interest expense after repayment of the ABL, lower other gains and charges, store consolidation and Brigit growth, and the headwinds are Acima volume, the excess cash flow sweep, Brigit deferred consideration of USD 37.5 million due by 2027-Q1, legal settlements and a term loan rate that reached 6.83% by 2026-10-22. On the supplied evidence these roughly offset, so leverage is more likely to hold near current levels than to fall much further unless Acima volume stabilises.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; 10-Q_2026-09-30_upbd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the issue is the 2029 refinancing: USD 495 million of notes and ABL drawings must be refinanced in 2028, against a term loan to 2032 whose springing terms are unseen. Sector headwinds are regulatory, with the federal regulator's December 2025 advisory opinion lowering federal risk for earned wage access while state action continues, and the lease-to-own model remains exposed to state and enforcement reclassification risk. Company tailwinds are Brigit scale and data-driven underwriting, which management describes but which the filings do not yet quantify.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer-specific downside begins with Acima volume continuing to fall at the third-quarter rate of 11.0% as retailer traffic and consumer payment behaviour weaken. The first operational break is lower Acima revenue and fewer early purchase options, which cut gross profit while store and occupancy costs stay fixed; charge-offs then rise, as they already have at Rent-A-Center. Replaying the FY2025 EBITDA decline of 12.76% lifts net leverage to 3.50x (3.56x pro forma for the dividend) and total debt to EBITDA to 3.85x, and interest cover falls below the 3.40x of FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity absorbs the shock: availability of USD 451.2 million exceeds identified twelve-month calls of USD 195.10 million, and management levers include cutting the dividend, which runs at USD 90.95 million a year, reducing merchandise purchases and closing stores. An unplanned settlement of USD 100 million adds 0.25x to leverage and would be met from availability. The binding constraint is not liquidity but refinancing in 2028 at higher leverage, with an unseen covenant and springing provisions, so resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress inside two years but not to guarantee refinancing on current terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Upbound presents an adequate business profile supported by two scaled lease-to-own platforms, a growing fintech segment and no sponsor, but credit quality is constrained by a shrinking Acima channel, legal exposure and thin interest cover. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because EBITDA recovered and capital intensity is low, but current free cash flow is flattered by working capital. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access in 2028 and on springing maturity terms that are not supplied. The primary downside path is Acima volume decline combined with settlement cash above the accrual. Further analysis would require ratings, covenant levels, the executed debt documents, the proxy statement and management projections. Fundamental credit completed with limitations. Top risk: Acima volume decline compounding legal settlement cost.
